Page-1/front-matter retraction check clean; full-text 'retract' scan zero hits. 538-page dense edited monograph => honest core-read of 100 pages: front matter pp. 1-14, ch. 9 quantitative CBF pp. 191-202, ch. 11 neurointensive care monitoring pp. 227-258, ch. 14 NIRS pp. 293-310, ch. 25 concussion metabolic recovery pp. 515-538 (all read in full via pymupdf text, page-anchored). Remaining 438 pages (pathogenesis chapters 1-8, MRI/impact-tech chapters 10/12/13, protection/management chapters 15-24) not deep-read; no primitives claimed from them. Source defects quarantined, no primitives built on them: (1) ch. 14 PDF math-glyph layer degraded - Eqs. (1)-(7) reconstructed from printed equations + defining prose, F*R dot prints as private-use U+F0E1 (preserved verbatim in p7 quote); (2) PRx described as 'digitised ICPs is divided with digitised MAPs' (p. 236) - loose phrasing for a slow-wave trend/correlation index; only the printed sign rule extracted; (3) p. 246 grammatical defect 'with irreversible damage occurs' preserved verbatim; (4) 'thomboxane' typo (p. 231) noted, not propagated. primitives.name: Cerebral perfusion pressure gradient (CPP = MAP - ICP) with autoregulatory operating corridor
primitives.verbatim_quote: In traumatic brain injury cases, the elevated ICP is the opposing force to the incoming mean systemic arterial pressure (MAP). Therefore, CPP in equation form can be stated as CPP = MAP – ICP.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: CPP, MAP, ICP: pressures, mmHg (printed). CBF: cerebral blood flow, ml blood per 100 g tissue per min (ml/100g/min, printed). CVR: cerebral vascular resistance, mmHg per (ml/100g/min) = mmHg*ml^-1*100g*min. The proportionality CBF ~ CPP/CVR is the printed statement 'CBF is proportional to CPP and inversely related to the cerebral vascular resistance' (p. 235); both sides dimensionally homogeneous. No dimensionless heuristic anywhere.
primitives.assumptions: Printed: elevated ICP is the opposing outflow force to incoming MAP; CPP equals the transmural pressure across cerebral vessel walls, the autoregulatory stimulus at the arteriolar level and the driving force for capillary fluid exchange (p. 235). The normal brain maintains constant flow by altering CVR within an autoregulatory corridor of '60 - 160 mmHg of MAP or CPP of 50 - 150 mmHg' (p. 235, en-dash as printed). Vasomotor effectors are controlled by CPP, metabolites, oxygen pressure, carbon dioxide pressure and temperature (p. 235). Steady-state pressure gradient; closed rigid cranium per Monro-Kellie (p2).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Autoregulation is often lost in the severely injured brain, making CBF pressure-passive (p. 235); excessive CPP can itself disturb autoregulation (Czosnyka 2001, cited p. 235) and drive hyperaemic insult, vasogenic oedema and further ICP rise (pp. 240, 248). As ICP approaches MAP, CPP tends to zero and flow ceases. The identity assumes ICP is the effective downstream pressure; it fails when jugular venous outflow pressure exceeds ICP. The corridor is population-level: 'the optimum CPP may vary considerably' between patients (p. 235).

layer2.mapping: Net driving gradient = applied drive minus opposing pressure, with a homeostatic corridor that keeps output flat while the regulator is intact and becomes pressure-passive when the regulator is impaired. In the 22-player football dynamical system this binds as a constraint on offensive control transitions: the protection scheme (regulator) holds clean-pocket output approximately constant across a corridor of defensive pressure; once the scheme's adaptive capacity is impaired (injuries, fatigue, identified tells), output becomes pressure-passive and 'raising CPP' - forcing more dropback volume - can worsen the very disruption it targets, exactly as aggressive CPP-targeted therapy worsens ICP in the impaired-autoregulation patient (pp. 240, 248). The invariant transported is the corridor plus the regime-dependent sign of the intervention, not any numeric football threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Play-by-play pressure/blitz flags vs pocket-collapse rate and EPA-per-dropback over rolling windows; scheme-change and injury reports identify regulator impairment. Calibrates the corridor and the regime switch. No sportsbook odds used.

primitives.name: Monro-Kellie doctrine: intracranial volume conservation with exhausted-compensation elastance
primitives.verbatim_quote: According to Monro-Kellie doctrine, the sum of the intracranial volumes of blood, brain and CSF is constant and that an increase in any one component must be offset by an equal decrease in another or else ICP rises.
primitives.latex: V_{\mathrm{blood}} + V_{\mathrm{brain}} + V_{\mathrm{CSF}} = \mathrm{const} \;\Rightarrow\; \Delta V_i = -\sum_{j \neq i} \Delta V_j \;\; \text{or} \;\; \mathrm{ICP} \uparrow
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: V_blood, V_brain, V_CSF: intracranial component volumes, mL. const: fixed craniospinal volume, mL. Delta V_i: volume change of component i, mL; the balance is a homogeneous volume equation (mL = mL). ICP: mmHg, appears only in the failure branch. Formalization of printed prose conservation rule; no source equation is printed for the doctrine.
primitives.assumptions: Formalization of the printed prose rule (no printed equation): rigid closed craniospinal compartment, incompressible contents; compensation first anatomical (CSF forced into the spinal dural sac), then functional (augment CBF) (p. 236). The doctrine is stated as a conservation constraint with an explicit failure branch ('or else ICP rises'), which is what makes it a sovereign logical invariant rather than a slogan.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Compensation exhausts: once anatomical and functional reserves are overstretched, the pressure-volume (elastance) curve steepens and small volume additions produce fast ICP rise with striking compliance loss - the decompensatory phase (p. 236, Fig. 4). Decompressive craniectomy deliberately violates the closed-compartment premise (pp. 241, 251); open sutures in infants likewise. The 'harmful compensatory' branches D/E/F (p. 237) show CBF augmentation itself raising ICP when autoregulation is impaired, so the functional defence can become the injury.

layer2.mapping: Fixed-total resource conservation with nonlinear compliance: the 22-player system operates under hard conserved totals (11 players per side per snap, fixed roster and snap budgets); adding volume to one compartment (extra rusher, heavier package) must be offset by equal subtraction elsewhere or the 'pressure' (exposure, fatigue, penalty risk) rises. While compensatory reserve exists (timeouts, depth, fresh legs) the addition is absorbed silently; once reserve is exhausted the same addition produces a disproportionate, fast pressure spike - the elastance-curve knee. Binds as a conservation constraint on substitution and package-transition kernels, and forbids any model that adds capability without accounting the offset.
layer2.telemetry: Snap counts by package, substitution logs, timeout/remaining-reserve state, penalty and pressure rates before/after reserve exhaustion; identifies the compliance knee. True fatigue reserve is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE without proxy calibration.

primitives.name: Cerebrovascular pressure reactivity index (PRx): correlation-sign regime classifier for autoregulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Positive trends signify impaired cerebral autoregulation whereas, negative and flattened trends denote intact autoregulation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: PRx: dimensionless cerebrovascular pressure reactivity index (trend/correlation of slow MAP and ICP waves; bounded [-1,1] in correlation form). MAP, ICP: mmHg. The extracted invariant is a predicate-logic sign rule (dimensionless implication), formalization of the printed trend rule; no dimensional equation is asserted.
primitives.assumptions: Formalization of the printed trend-sign rule (pp. 236-238): positive MAP-ICP association implies impaired autoregulation; negative or flattened association implies intact vasoconstrictive response to MAP surges. The chapter describes PRx operationally as 'digitised ICPs is divided with digitised MAPs and focusing on their trends or values' (p. 236) and cites Smielewski et al. 1997 and Zweifel et al. 2008 for continuous monitoring; the sovereign invariant extracted here is the sign rule, which is what the text actually uses to gate ICP-vs-CPP therapy choice (p. 247).
primitives.breakdown_regime: SOURCE DEFECT quarantined: the 'divided with' phrasing is a loose description of a slow-wave trend/correlation index, not a literal instantaneous ratio; no primitive is built on the ratio reading. The sign rule requires slow-wave trend windows and is confounded by CO2 reactivity, sedation, vasospasm and temperature (vasomotor effectors, p. 235). Lee 2001 (cited p. 235) shows CO2 reactivity, pressure autoregulation and metabolic suppression reactivity dissociate after injury, and elevated ICP affects all tested components - so a single index cannot stand for all vasoreactivity.

layer2.mapping: Derived regime-classifier kernel: estimate the sign of the coupling between an applied pressure series and the system's disturbance series over a rolling window, then select the control law by regime - positive coupling (pressure-passive) implies reduce exposure ('ICP-targeted': quicker releases, max-protect, run-heavy); non-positive coupling (regulated) implies drive may be raised ('CPP-targeted'). This is a derived kernel, not a printed football law: it transports the PRx sign rule into the protection-scheme control problem, where opponent blitz rate is the MAP analogue and pressure-allowed/pocket-collapse rate is the ICP analogue. The regime decision precedes any EV comparison of play calls.
layer2.telemetry: Rolling-window correlation of opponent blitz/pressure rate with pressure-allowed and sack rate from play-by-play; regime flips validated against scheme and injury changes. Requires several drives per window; single-snap ratios are inadmissible (mirrors the slow-wave requirement).

primitives.name: Ischemic CBF threshold cascade: electrical failure precedes irreversible membrane failure
primitives.verbatim_quote: The normal CBF is 45 to 55 ml/100g/min, and the electrical function is impaired (isoelectric silence) if CBF is < 23 ml/100g/min with irreversible damage occurs if CBF is < 8 ml/100g/min.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: CBF: ml blood per 100 g tissue per min (ml/100g/min, printed). Thresholds 45-55 (normal band), 23 (electrical failure), 8 (irreversible damage) all in ml/100g/min as printed. Predicates dimensionless; interval formalization of printed numeric thresholds, no derived equation.
primitives.assumptions: Printed population thresholds under coupled flow-metabolism conditions (p. 246, citing Jordan 1993; Procaccio et al. 2001). The interval between electrical failure and irreversible damage defines electrically silent but potentially viable tissue. The source sentence carries a grammatical defect ('with irreversible damage occurs') preserved verbatim per source-defect rule; thresholds are quoted as printed, not re-derived or smoothed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The statement is not duration-aware: time-at-flow determines whether silent tissue survives (penumbra logic; ch. 9 cites Astrup, Siesjo & Symon 1981 'Thresholds in cerebral ischemia - the ischemic penumbra', p. 199). Hypothermia and metabolic suppression lower demand and shift effective thresholds (ch. 11 section 9, p. 250). The electrical threshold is an EEG observable while the irreversible threshold is a tissue-fate observable - different measurement channels, so the cascade cannot be read off a single monitor. Probe location (peri-contusional vs intact cortex) changes the reading.
timescales: tau_0=electrical silence onset (seconds-minutes at low flow)
tau_2=irreversible membrane failure (hours at profound ischemia)

layer2.mapping: Two-tier failure with a rescue window: a system can be functionally silent (output collapsed) yet structurally intact, and only a lower, slower threshold marks irreversible loss. In football operations this binds return-to-load decisions: a unit or player below the performance threshold is 'electrically silent' (benched, deactivated) but recoverable if load is withdrawn before the structural-injury threshold. In DFS/portfolio terms a strategy in drawdown may be functionally stopped-out while its edge capital is intact - reactivation is admissible only inside the rescue window, and the two thresholds must never be collapsed into one. The invariant is the ordered pair of thresholds plus the viability window between them.
layer2.telemetry: Snap-load and fatigue proxies vs injury reports (structural threshold); strategy drawdown vs realized edge decay (functional vs structural). The window between thresholds is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE without a viability marker - the source's lesson is precisely that a second observable (EEG/microdialysis there, objective load telemetry here) is required.

primitives.name: NAA synthesis energy cost: net loss of 11 ATP per NAA; acetyl-CoA hydrolysis Delta-G = -31.2 kJ/mol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Since the oxidative phosphorylation is stoichiometrically coupled to the amount of electron transferred to molecular oxygen by the electron transport chain, the final result will be a net loss of 11 ATP molecules for each NAA molecule newly synthesized.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Delta G: molar Gibbs energy of acetyl-CoA hydrolysis, kJ/mol (printed -31.2, p. 518). cost_NAA: dimensionless molecule-count ratio, 11 ATP forgone per 1 NAA synthesized (printed). NADH, FADH2: reducing-equivalent counts, dimensionless (3 and 1, printed). NAA concentration ~10 mmol/l brain water; turnover ~0.75 mmol per l brain water per hour, regenerated 1.8 times per 24 h (all printed p. 518). Energy and count ledgers kept separate; no cross-unit arithmetic.
primitives.assumptions: Printed stoichiometric argument (p. 518, repeated p. 529): acetyl-CoA diverted to ANAT-catalyzed acetylation of aspartate does not enter the Krebs cycle, forfeiting 3 NADH + 1 FADH2; oxidative phosphorylation is assumed stoichiometrically coupled to electron transfer to molecular oxygen, giving the net 11-ATP loss per NAA. NAA homeostasis balances three velocities: neuronal biosynthesis, neuronal outflow to extracellular space, oligodendrocyte uptake/degradation via ASPA (Baslow 2003, cited p. 518). NAA synthesis is strictly dependent on neuronal energy state and mitochondrial functioning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The 11-ATP figure assumes full oxidative yield of the forgone reducing equivalents (implicit P/O coupling); after concussion, mitochondrial dysfunction plus nicotinic-coenzyme pool depletion (NAD+/NADH, NADP+/NADPH hydrolysis via hydroxyl radical or NAD-glycohydrolase, PARP activation; pp. 528-529) lower actual yield, so the printed cost is a floor on the true energetic burden. NAA's biochemical role is explicitly unsettled in the source (molecular water pump vs acetate donor for myelin vs NAAG precursor hypotheses, p. 518). Rodent repeat-injury boundary (p. 526): two concussions 3 days apart compose into irreversible sTBI-like cumulative damage; spaced 5 days they are fully reversible and act as separate events - a source-specific calibration of the vulnerability window, not a human constant.
timescales: tau_3=repeat-injury vulnerability window (days; 3 vs 5 day rodent boundary)

layer2.mapping: Derived vulnerability kernel: recovery is itself an energy-consuming process, so during homeostasis restoration the system's margin against a second perturbation is minimized, and two insults inside the recovery window compose super-linearly (cumulative, potentially irreversible) while the same insults outside it compose as independent events. Transported to football: the return-to-play clock must be driven by completion of the repair process (metabolic telemetry), not by elapsed time or symptom report; a second hit inside the window is a different, heavier-tailed event than the first. The kernel is the interval-dependent composition rule for repeated shocks, derived from the printed bioenergetics and the 3-day/5-day rodent contrast.
layer2.telemetry: 1H-MRS NAA/Cr time course in the source (frontal white-matter voxel, 3.0 T, TE=144 ms, TR=2000 ms, p. 521); in GSE, objective recovery markers (load tolerance, repeated-impact response) gate re-exposure. Symptom report alone is inadmissible (see p6).

primitives.name: Symptom-metabolism dissociation: return-to-play gated on NAA/Cr normalization, not symptom clearance
primitives.verbatim_quote: Moreover, in our previous studies we showed that the time to return the NAA/Cr to normal cerebral levels in singly concussed athletes is within 30 days post- impact. In the present cohort of doubly concussed athletes, the time required to measure values of the NAA/Cr ratio similar to those recorded in controls after the second concussion was of 81.2 ± 24.4 days.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: NAA/Cr: dimensionless 1H-MRS peak-area ratio (Gaussian-fitted areas, p. 521). t: days post-injury. Printed cohort values: single-concussion NAA/Cr normalization within 30 days; double-concussion 81.2 +/- 24.4 days (p. 528); symptom duration 5.8 +/- 2.1 days after 1st vs 41.2 +/- 13.0 days after 2nd concussion, p<0.001 (pp. 521-522); second-impact NAA/Cr -23.6% vs controls (p. 522). Predicate-logic formalization of the printed clinical decision rule; no source equation is printed.
primitives.assumptions: Formalization of the printed decision rule (pp. 526-528): restriction from physical activity is mandatory until NAA normalization; the proposed 4-step timetable gates activity intensity on serial MRS (rest ~days 1-15, graded activity ~16-22, intensification ~23-30, return to play at normal NAA ~day 30). Semi-quantitative MRS assumes Cr and Cho are unvarying internal references (p. 519) - an explicit modeling assumption of the source, not a verified invariant. Cohorts: 40 concussed athletes + 30 controls (multicenter, Vagnozzi 2010) and 6 doubly-concussed athletes (present study).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Reference instability: if Cr/Cho themselves shift after injury the ratio misleads (assumption acknowledged p. 519). Small n (6 double-concussion cases); self-reported symptoms and concealed training restarts (patients 1-6 resumed at 13-17% NAA/Cr deficit, pp. 523-525) bias the symptom arm. The <=30-day single-concussion figure is cohort-specific, not a universal constant; 81.2 +/- 24.4 days has wide spread. SIS existence is contested in the source itself (McCrory 2001; McCrory & Berkovic 2001, cited p. 517); the authors' broadened SIS definition (symptom-metabolism disproportion after repeat concussion, pp. 527-528) is a proposal, not established fact, and is labeled as such.
timescales: tau_2=NAA fast recovery phase (~10-15 days; single-concussion normalization <=30 days)

layer2.mapping: Latent-state gating invariant: disappearance of surface symptoms is not evidence that the hidden state has recovered, and decisions gated on the observable alone select precisely the agents most likely to fail - athletes who feel fine restart at a 13-17% metabolic deficit and are re-concussed, after which symptoms last 41.2 vs 5.8 days and metabolic recovery ~2.7x longer. Isomorphic to any reactivation decision in the engine: a strategy, model, or player cleared by surface metrics while a latent viability marker is still abnormal must remain restricted; the gate is the latent marker's return to its control range, with the observable used only as a necessary, never sufficient, condition. This is the source's central sovereign lesson for return-to-play and for strategy reactivation alike.
layer2.telemetry: Serial 1H-MRS NAA/Cr vs control range (source); symptom inventory as auxiliary channel only. In GSE: pre-declared objective reactivation criteria per flagged strategy/player, verified against held-out data; no odds inputs.

primitives.name: Fick-principle tracer kinetics: CBF from the deconvolved impulse residue function F*R(t)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The initial height of the function FR(t) is CBF, as by definition R(0) = 1, and the area under the curve is the cerebral blood volume (CBV) (Brown et al., 2002).
primitives.latex: \frac{dQ(t)}{dt} = F\,C_a(t) - F\,C_v(t); \qquad Q(t) = C_a(t) * [F\,R(t)], \quad R(0)=1; \qquad F\,R(0) = \mathrm{CBF}, \quad \int_0^{\infty} F\,R(t)\,dt = \mathrm{CBV}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Q(t): tissue tracer amount, mass (e.g. mg). Ca(t), Cv(t): arterial/venous tracer concentration, mass/volume (mg/ml). F: blood flow, ml/100g/min. R(t): dimensionless impulse residue function, R(0)=1 by definition. *: convolution. t: min. CBV: cerebral blood volume, ml blood/100g tissue; brain density rho=1.05 g/ml converts volume/mass to volume/volume (p. 297). CMRO2 = F*AVDO2 (Eq. 4, p. 296): mlO2/100g/min with AVDO2 in mlO2/100ml blood (normal ~6.5; CMRO2 ~3.2, p. 243). All terms dimensionally homogeneous; equations reconstruct printed Eqs. (1)-(4) whose glyph layer is degraded (see assumptions).
primitives.assumptions: Printed Fick conservation (Meier & Zierler 1954, cited p. 295): tissue tracer change equals arterial inflow minus venous outflow; venous concentration is the arterial input convolved with the organ impulse response h(t) (Eq. 2); Q = Ca * (F*R) (Eq. 3, Lee 2002). Initial plateau height of F*R is CBF because R(0)=1; its area is CBV (p. 296). LaTeX reconstructs Eqs. (1)-(4) from the printed equations plus their defining prose because the PDF math-glyph layer is degraded (the F*R dot prints as private-use glyph U+F0E1, preserved verbatim in the quote). CMRO2 via Fick additionally assumes the 20/10/70 arterial/capillary/venous CBV split and capillary Hb = mean(arterial, venous) (pp. 296-297), plus 1.39 ml O2/gHb oxygen capacity (Eq. 6, p. 297).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Deconvolution is noise-sensitive and ill-posed; extracerebral (scalp/skull/CSF) contamination makes single-channel continuous-wave NIRS underdetermined and biases CBF low (pp. 303-304); homogeneous-head or population-average layer assumptions are inaccurate in most clinical situations (p. 305). Vascular-bed stationarity is assumed during the bolus; vasospasm and autoregulation failure violate it. TOI alone is a poor CBF surrogate: reported normal range 60-85% overlaps the change attributed to ischemia (p. 295). Validation precision CBF 9.71%, CBV 13.05% (p. 299) and CMRO2 10.7% (p. 300) were obtained in newborn piglets, not adult humans; CMRO2 falls only when CBF drops below ~25 ml/100g/min because oxygen extraction compensates (p. 302).
timescales: tau_0=ICG bolus passage and sampling (200 ms spectra; ~50 s curves)
tau_2=bedside repeat measurement and PaCO2 reactivity tests (minutes-hours)
tau_3=therapeutic-window detection in neonatal HI (<=6 h)

layer2.mapping: Derived system-identification kernel: from an input concentration series and a tissue response series, deconvolve the transport kernel F*R(t); its initial height is instantaneous throughput and its integral is inventory (volume). Transported to the football dynamical system: treat a drive's snap sequence as the input and the yards/EP response as the tissue curve; the deconvolved kernel separates the offense's transport efficiency (initial height = immediate throughput per snap) from accumulated inventory (drive-level EP stock), with the opponent's impulse response playing the role of the vascular transit-time distribution. Explicitly a derived identification recipe, not a printed football law; it inherits the source's stationarity and contamination warnings as admissibility conditions.
layer2.telemetry: Play-by-play snap-to-outcome sequences per drive; kernel estimates require repeated drives against similar defensive fronts (stationarity analogue). The source's warning that uncalibrated priors (layer thickness there, opponent-front priors here) break the estimate transfers directly; depth-resolved/time-resolved priors are the calibration path.

reasoning_traces.think: The central trap in this chapter is that the same intervention has opposite signs in two regimes, and the regime is hidden. Start from the printed invariant: CPP = MAP - ICP (p. 235), with CBF proportional to CPP and inversely related to CVR. In the intact brain, autoregulation holds flow constant across a corridor of 60-160 mmHg MAP or 50-150 mmHg CPP by adjusting CVR; the pressure gradient is a stimulus the regulator answers, not a command the tissue obeys. After severe TBI the regulator is variably destroyed: Lee 2001 (cited p. 235) shows pressure autoregulation is variably impaired while CO2 reactivity stays relatively intact and metabolic suppression reactivity stays severely impaired, and elevated ICP damages all tested components. Once the regulator fails, the tissue becomes pressure-passive, and here the vicious circle closes: raising MAP to raise CPP now raises ICP as well, because the dilated, unregulated vascular bed transmits the pressure into a closed Monro-Kellie compartment (p. 236). The chapter's Figure 5 labels these harmful compensatory branches D, E, F: increased CBF causing increment in ICP, 'commonly induced by clinicians' (p. 237). Young 2003's aggressive CPP management produced good outcomes in four patients with extremely high ICP, yet other patients with high CPP or aggressive CPP management developed cerebral oedema and poor outcomes (p. 240). Same lever, opposite results, because the hidden state differs. The resolution the chapter builds is a regime classifier before any therapy choice: PRx, the trend coupling of MAP and ICP. Positive trends signify impaired autoregulation; negative or flattened trends denote intact autoregulation (p. 238). With intact autoregulation, CPP-targeted therapy aims CPP > 50 mmHg, commonly 60-70; with impaired autoregulation the target is inverted - keep CPP below 50-60 mmHg, and Johnson 2011 found favorable outcomes precisely there (p. 247). The decision procedure is therefore: classify the regime from the sign of the slow-wave coupling, then choose ICP-targeted versus CPP-targeted therapy, then watch for the time-shift from compensatory to decompensatory or harmful compensatory phase using multimodality cross-validation (SjVO2 > 75% warning of hyperaemia, TCD trends, Licox, microdialysis; pp. 247-248). Transported to the 22-player system, the structure is identical and the failure mode is identical. A protection scheme is an autoregulator: while it is intact, clean-pocket output stays roughly flat across a corridor of defensive pressure, and the coordinator can raise 'CPP' - more dropbacks, deeper routes - without paying for it. When the regulator is impaired (tackle injured, fatigue accumulated, the defense has identified the slide protection's tell), the same increase in drive volume transmits directly into disruption: pressure-allowed rises with blitz rate, the pocket collapses faster, and the quarterback's internal clock is forced into the exact hurried decisions the defense wants. The high-EV call in the aggregate - 'our pass game wins games, throw more' - is the aggressive CPP push, and in the impaired regime it is the mechanism of the loss, not the remedy. The derived kernel is the PRx sign test on play-by-play: correlate opponent pressure rate with our disruption rate over rolling windows; positive coupling means reduce exposure (quicker releases, max protect, run-heavy - the ICP-targeted analogue), non-positive coupling means the drive corridor is open. The veto is absolute: no EV comparison of play calls is admissible before the regime is classified, because the EV table itself was estimated in the wrong regime. This is also why the chapter insists monitoring alone does not change outcome (p. 227): the classifier must be wired to a therapy that exists, otherwise it is telemetry without control. In engine terms, a regime flag that cannot trigger an abstention or a control-law switch is decoration. The Monro-Kellie conservation law supplies the second veto: any package that adds pressure exposure without an offsetting subtraction somewhere else is spending compensatory reserve, and once the reserve is exhausted the elastance knee turns small additions into fast, disproportionate pressure spikes - the fourth-quarter collapse that looks sudden but was prepaid snap by snap.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The hidden state here was created by a specific historical scar: the failure of pharmacological neuroprotection. Narayan's 2002 review (cited p. 229) concluded most neuroprotective trials failed to show robust efficacy, which pushed the field from 'protect the neuron with a drug' to 'monitor the physical regime and titrate the physical inputs' - ICP, CPP, flow, oxygen. Lundberg's 1965 plateau waves (50-100 mmHg, 5-20 minutes, p. 238) were the first telemetry that revealed the compensatory vasodilation could itself become the injury, and Bouma 1992's finding that about one-third of head-injured patients had low CBF early (p. 235) broke the assumption that raised ICP always meant hyperaemia. Each scar left a sediment: the corridor, the sign rule, the multimodality cross-validation. The lineage matters because it explains why the chapter distrusts single numbers: every single-number protocol (ICP-only, CPP-only) was born from a cohort where the hidden regime happened to be uniform, and failed when it was not.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Recursive belief clash under pressure: the neurointensivist sees a CPP of 45 and feels the comfort of a number below target, reaching for the pressor - the CPP-targeted reflex trained by guidelines. The patient's impaired autoregulation 'believes' otherwise: every mmHg of MAP now arrives as intracranial volume. The clinician must model his own trained reflex as an adversary and ask what the PRx trend says before the reflex fires. The football analogue is exact: the coordinator sees third-and-long and feels the comfort call - his best pass concept, the one that won last week - while the defensive coordinator has spent the week building a tendency trap for precisely that concept in precisely that down-distance. The quarterback's internal clock, already shortened by two sacks, is a third belief state: he will throw early to a read that is not there. Each agent must model the others' comfort reflexes: the DC models the coordinator's tendency, the coordinator models the QB's panic clock, and the quarterback models the protection's actual (not nominal) slide. The regime classifier is what lets the coordinator override his own comfort call with evidence instead of hope.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Cross-layer adjudication: physics vetoes the high-EV call whenever the Monro-Kellie compartment is near its elastance knee and PRx is positive. In that regime the expected-value table computed from pressure-passive-free data is invalid, because the intervention changes the very coupling it was conditioned on; the physically admissible action set shrinks to exposure-reduction, and any call outside it is vetoed regardless of its nominal EV. Psychology adds a second veto: the comfort call is selected precisely when the decision-maker is most threatened, so the subjective confidence in the call is anti-correlated with its admissibility. The adjudication rule is lexicographic: regime classification first, conservation-reserve check second, EV comparison only inside the surviving set. A veto is not a suggestion to discount the EV; it removes the option from the choice set, exactly as the chapter removes aggressive CPP therapy from the impaired-autoregulation patient's menu (p. 247).

reasoning_traces.think: The second sovereign structure in this book is the dissociation between an observable recovery signal and the latent state that actually governs safety, and the catastrophic composition rule when a second shock arrives inside the latent recovery window. The bioenergetic anchor is printed twice (pp. 518, 529): NAA synthesis consumes acetyl-CoA whose hydrolysis carries Delta-G = -31.2 kJ/mol, and because that acetyl-CoA then cannot enter the Krebs cycle, the cell forfeits 3 NADH and 1 FADH2, a net loss of 11 ATP per NAA molecule synthesized. NAA is not a passive marker: it is ~10 mmol/l brain water, regenerated 1.8 times per 24 hours at ~0.75 mmol/l/hour, and its resynthesis is strictly coupled to mitochondrial recovery. So after concussion, the brain must pay an energy tax to rebuild the very molecule that signals neuronal wealth, while mitochondrial dysfunction and nicotinic-coenzyme depletion (NADH/NADPH hydrolysis, PARP activation, pp. 528-529) are simultaneously suppressing the energy supply. Recovery is expensive exactly when the budget is smallest - that is the mechanistic content of Hovda's 'window of metabolic vulnerability' (Giza & Hovda 2001, cited p. 517). The human telemetry makes the dissociation quantitative. In the multicenter cohort of 40 concussed athletes, symptom clearance was self-declared between 3 and 15 days, while NAA/Cr normalization took up to 30 days, with a slow phase of ~15-20 days then a faster ~10-15 day phase (pp. 520, 528). Symptoms vanish weeks before metabolism is safe. The six doubly-concussed athletes show what happens when behavior is gated on the observable: every one restarted training after symptom clearance while NAA/Cr was still 13-17% below controls (pp. 523-525), and every one was re-concussed. After the second impact, NAA/Cr fell to -23.6% versus controls, near severe-TBI values (p. 522); symptoms lasted 41.2 +/- 13.0 days versus 5.8 +/- 2.1 after the first (p<0.001), and metabolic normalization took 81.2 +/- 24.4 days versus <=30 for a single concussion (p. 528). The rodent boundary sharpens the composition rule: two mild injuries 3 days apart produce irreversible, cumulative, severe-TBI-like metabolic damage; the same two injuries 5 days apart are fully reversible and act as separate events (p. 526). Inside the window, shocks compose super-linearly; outside, they compose additively. The decision invariant the authors extract is a gate, not a guideline: restriction from physical activity until NAA normalization, with a 4-step MRS-driven timetable (rest ~1-15 days, graded activity ~16-22, intensification ~23-30, return to play at normal NAA ~30 days; p. 528). The general kernel transports cleanly to any reactivation decision under hidden damage. A strategy stopped out of a portfolio, a model pulled after a failure, a player benched after a knock - all present an observable 'symptom clearance' (drawdown stopped, error rate back to baseline, player says he feels fine) while the latent viability marker (edge decay, calibration drift, metabolic or load-tolerance state) is still abnormal. Gating reactivation on the observable alone is adverse selection: the agents most eager to declare recovery are precisely those whose latent state is worst, because the observable is cheap to fake and the latent state is expensive to rebuild. The athlete who restarts at a 16% NAA deficit is the strategy that re-levers at the first green day. The veto is bioenergetic before it is statistical: inside the vulnerability window the second shock is a different distribution with a catastrophic tail (second impact syndrome, malignant oedema, pp. 517, 527), so no expected-value computation that treats the second shock as an independent copy of the first is admissible. The source is honest about its own limits - SIS existence is contested (McCrory 2001), the broadened SIS definition is a proposal, n=6 is small, and Cr/Cho reference stability is an assumption - and those limits travel with the kernel: the gate must use a pre-declared, reference-stable latent marker with its own control range, never a ratio whose denominator can itself be injured.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This invariant descends from a chain of underestimation scars. Saunders & Harbaugh 1984 named second impact syndrome in contact sports (cited p. 517); for decades the 'mild' label - normal CT, normal MRI, GCS 14-15 - made concussion invisible to the imaging era, and the book documents the consequence: hematomas diagnosed with a median 18-hour delay, only 50% of mildly injured US patients with documented neurological observations (p. 516). Hovda's rodent work (1993) and the Giza & Hovda 2001 neurometabolic cascade created the hidden-state concept; the Catania/Tor Vergata group's ATP and NAA measurements (Vagnozzi 1999-2010, Tavazzi 2005-2007) gave it a price in ATP; the 1H-MRS multicenter trial gave it a bedside-adjacent observable. Each generation inherited the previous one's blind spot: imaging era missed metabolism, symptom era missed the window. The 3-day/5-day rodent boundary is the sediment of that lineage - a measured composition rule, not a folk warning.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Three agents, three incentive-distorted belief states. The athlete knows his roster spot decays while he sits, so his symptom report is a strategic signal, not a measurement - the book's patients literally concealed their training restarts (pp. 523-525). The coach knows the star's replacement is worse and models the athlete's report as truth because believing it is convenient; his comfort call is 'he says he's fine, and he looks fine.' The physician must model both: the athlete's incentive to under-report and the coach's incentive to believe, and recognize that her own observable (symptom inventory) is the channel both adversaries are gaming. The recursive move is to stop negotiating over the cheap signal and move the decision to an expensive, hard-to-fake channel - serial NAA/Cr against a control range - which is exactly what the 4-step timetable does. In the engine, the same triangle appears when a strategy's owner declares it 'fixed' after a quiet week: the owner's incentive, the portfolio manager's convenience belief, and the auditor's duty to gate on held-out latent telemetry rather than the owner's symptom report.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The bioenergetic layer vetoes the high-EV return unconditionally inside the window: returning the star wins more games in expectation only if the second-impact tail is ignored, and the printed composition rule (3-day spacing irreversible, 5-day reversible; 81.2 vs <=30 days metabolic recovery) says the tail is not a small correction but a regime change. Psychology vetoes the symptom-based gate because the reporting channel is adversarially selected. The adjudication is lexicographic again: latent-marker normalization is a hard constraint; expected value is optimized only over the set of decisions that satisfy it. Where the latent marker is unavailable, the honest action is abstention - continued restriction - not interpolation from symptoms, mirroring the source's insistence that no currently available diagnostic test measures the metabolic vulnerability state (p. 527) and that MRS, not feeling, must drive the timetable.

universal_lens: Polymath audit lens: any constrained flow system under injury obeys a triad - a conservation law with exhausted-compensation nonlinearity (Monro-Kellie), a regime classifier that must precede control-law selection (PRx sign rule), and a latent-state gate that forbids reactivation on surface-symptom clearance (NAA window). Audit any decision system by asking: where is the conserved total, where is the hidden regime, and which cheap observable is being mistaken for the expensive latent state?
gsi_mapping: GSI (fluid/axonal shear, bioenergetics, clinical telemetry): CPP = MAP - ICP is the perfusion driving gradient whose failure produces axonal shear vulnerability and ischemic cascades; PRx is the bedside autoregulation assay; NAA/Cr via 1H-MRS is the axonal/mitochondrial wealth telemetry (11 ATP per NAA resynthesis, Delta-G -31.2 kJ/mol); the CBF 23/8 threshold cascade separates reversible electrical silence from irreversible membrane failure, and the 6-hour neonatal HI therapeutic window (p. 301) is the clinical-telemetry deadline that makes early CMRO2 detection decisive.
gse_mapping: GSE (Coach-Mind sim, deception, DFS/portfolio tail risk): the PRx sign rule becomes the regime classifier that gates ICP-vs-CPP-style control-law selection before any play-call EV comparison; Monro-Kellie becomes the roster/snap conservation constraint with an elastance knee; the symptom-metabolism dissociation becomes the strategy/player reactivation gate (latent telemetry, not surface clearance), and the 3-day/5-day composition rule is the correlated-tail-risk kernel: a second shock inside the vulnerability window is a regime change, not an independent draw. Deception enters as the adversarial symptom-report channel (athlete, strategy owner) that the gate must bypass. No odds inputs; internal only.
